J U D G M E N T

/ AWAR D (Under Section 26 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894)
1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 LAC no. 316/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW))
Inder Pal & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 2 of 12 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, Government intended to acquire about 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3. The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (19)/2001/L&B/LA/28176 dated 19.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi.

entities.text: Inder Pal & Ors. v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The LAC (N/W)

after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 2480 bighas 01 biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.

4. It is stated that the petitioners are the recorded owner/bhumidhar of the land comprised in Khasra no. 9/7 (416), 10/10 (412), 11 (412), 11/15 (416), 26/13 Min (36), 17/1 (35), 18min (36), 23/1/1 Min (113), 24/2 (33), 30/4/2 (410), 5 (412), 7 (416) i.e. total area 52 Bigha and 03 Biswas in which the share of the petitioner no. 1 and 2 is 1/3rd each and share of petitioners no. 3 to 5 is 1/9th each and in addition to the above LAC no. 316/ 2016 (Award No. 16/2005 06/DC(NW)) Inder Pal & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 3 of 12 mentioned land bearing no. 30/4/1 (006) which was a permanent well and the share of petitioner in this land was 1/6th share each of petitioner no. 1 and 2 and 1/18th share each of petitioner no. 3 to 5, situated in the revenue estate of Village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi (in short, the said land).
5.

sentences.text:
It is stated that the Award passed by the ld. LAC is not acceptable to the petitioners and,
therefore, this reference has been filed with a view to reassess the market value of the land which has been arbitrarily assessed by the LAC without taking into account the fertility, potentiality,
surroundings and topography under acquisition.

The said land is levelled land and is situated in a belt which has not experienced any major earthquake, flood or any other natural calamity for the last more than hundred years and is best suited for all sorts of land uses like residential,
commercial, industrial and agricultural etc. the quality of the said land makes it most suitable in the state of Delhi.

sentences.text: It is stated that the said land falls in the most fertile belt of Delhi and the petitioners are cultivating the said land and are growing three crops in a year "fasali year".

Whole of the said land is having welldeveloped irrigation system having borwell, tubewells and canal system linked with Yamuna Canal and all crops including cereals, vegetables crops, oil yielding crops and sugarcane are being cultivated by the petitioners and the income per acre is more than Rs. 2 lakhs per year.

In addition to it, the petitioners are having milk yielding cattles which are fully fed by the land LAC no.
316/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Inder Pal & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 4 of 12 produce and all the daily needs of the petitioners are fulfilled by the said land.

sentences.text: 7. It is stated that the petitioners shall be forced to change from one mode of life i.e. agro based lifestyle to modern lifestyle due to the acquisition of the said land and the new lifestyle has become more expensive, and the daily inflation shall have an adverse economic effect on the petitioners, who were selfreliant before acquisition of the said land.
The said land acquired by the ld. LAC is surrounded by the residential as well as industrial areas.
The area under acquisition is having mettled roads, and is having a very good connectivity with other areas of Delhi.
The National Highway10 is just 1 km away from the revenue estate of Village Rani Khera and the railway line from Delhi Junction to Firozpur is just half kilometres away.

The infrastructure in the vicinity of the land of the petitioners is already in existence i.e. electricity, schools, residential areas and industrial areas, have been developed which has enhanced the market value of the said land.

8. It is stated that the land under acquisition including the said land is having better location than the revenue estate of Village like Karala, Savda, Madanpur Dabas, Mundaka, Ghewra and Hiran Koodna, etc which falls on the NorthWestern and SouthWestern side of the revenue estate of village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi where sale instances show constant rise in the land rates

, however,
those lands are far away from village Rani Khera, if LAC no. 316/ 2016 (Award No. 16/2005 06/DC(NW)) Inder Pal & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 5 of 12 the distance from the urban limits of Delhi state are taken into consideration.

entities.text: Inder Pal & Ors. v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said land has great potentiality and is fit for supporting high rise buildings, and other residential infrastructure with a lesser investment, if compared with the development work carried out in South Delhi and East Delhi, where the land was hilly, terrain and low line respectively, which require a huge amount for levelling and making the land usable for construction activities.

The ld. LAC has overlooked the facts while determining the market value of the said land, in as much as, if all the factors are taken together for assessing the market value of the land under acquisition, it shall be Rs. 1 crore per acre or at least Rs. 2000/ per square yard.

If the said land under acquisition is auctioned to the private developers, they would have purchased the same for more than Rs. 1 crore per acre, which fact finds support from the fact that the land bordering Delhi, particularly in the village Kundli and Kasar in Haryana, has shown a very fast increase in the land prices due to participation of private builders, however, the land of Village Kundli and Kasar is comparatively inferior to the land under acquisition.

9. It is stated that in view of these facts and circumstances and keeping in view the consideration of the petitioners, petitioners are claiming market value of Rs. 2000/ per sq. yards or Rs. 1 crores per acre in addition to the said market value.
The petitioners have also claimed solatium @ 30% and additional amount @ 12% and further claim interest @ 9% and 15% as per the provisions of the Act.

During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 05.09.2023 and Ld.

22. The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.

rpc_texts: The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Savitri Devi (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,45,800/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/ per acre.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.

As per the forwarding letter vide which the reference petition was referred to this Court, the possession of 10/10 (412), 26/13 Min (306), 17/1 (305), 18 Min (306), 23/1 Min (113), 24/2 (303), 30//4/2 (410) has not been taken.
Therefore, the petitioners will not be entitled for any compensation qua the said land.
LAC no. 316/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Inder Pal & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 11 of 12 24.

In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs: (1) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,45,800/- per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre is accordingly accorded.

(2)
Additional amount @ 12% ( in terms of Section 23 (1A) of the Act).

(3) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation (in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(4) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
